body: The temple is an exceptional site with various parts dedicated to explaining different aspects of Buddha's life through fairy-tale-like statues in rich, vibrant colors. The Hell area within the temple is depicted in a way that conveys a sense of overflow and eeriness, creating a truly impactful experience for visitors. Overall, the temple is a fantastic destination to explore and is considered a highlight for many visitors to Sri Lanka.
title: Exceptional temple!

body: Very beautiful temple, interesting 7 story ascent with inside the highest Buddha of SriLanka, impressive depiction of demons if one violates the 7 rules. Only the attitude of the elephant is terrible and unworthy. It's too bad.
title: Very nice to look at

body: Wewurukannala Vihara (often spelled Wawrukannala Temple) is one of the most unusual and memorable Buddhist temples in southern Sri Lanka. Located near Dikwella, the temple is famous for its towering seated Buddha statue and its vivid, thought-provoking depictions of Buddhist teachings.
title: The most beautiful temple

body: After reading many reviews that an elephant is chained up here (20 years!?!!!) I will not visit. Free this poor elephant and let it live the rest of its life in one of your beautiful parks / if not possible to rehabilitate to the wild to a large enclosure. Stop this animal cruelty in a Buddhist temple of all places. Please!
title: Animal cruelty

body: They call this place a temple, yet for years they have kept an elephant chained there. The animal cannot walk, cannot sit or lie down properly. This is outright cruelty. This place has nothing to do with Buddhist philosophy or holiness.DO NOT GO there. Do not support animal abuse. Sri Lanka has many other temples that do not exploit and torture animals for profit.
title: Animal abuse and cruelty

body: I have visited Wewurukannala Vihara temple. The place is architecturally spectacular and has enormous spiritual and cultural potential. However, my experience was marked by deep sadness and outrage.For more than 20 years, the temple has been keeping an elephant chained on three of its legs, without real freedom of movement. The state of this animal is clearly cruel and incompatible with any principle of compassion. It is especially incomprehensible and painful that this should happen in a Buddhist monastery, a religion that preaches respect, non-violence and compassion to all living things.In addition, the monastery grounds are very dirty and unkempt, which contrasts greatly with how splendid they could be if cared for properly. It is a real pity to see how a place with such spiritual and touristic value is marred by abandonment and lack of sensitivity.Hopefully those responsible will reflect and take urgent action: free the elephant, guarantee its royal welfare and take care of the temple environment. Only then can this place be aligned with the values it claims to represent and become a truly dignified, respectful and compassionate space.
title: ANIMAL ABUSE

body: So disturbed by the chained elephant. After complaining to the officials we learned that the poor elephant is permanently chained and clearly very distressed. What a crying shame at the temple would be beautiful otherwise.
title: Chained Elephant

body: DO NOT VISIT - Arjuna the elephant is kept chained up day after day. The sight of this magnificent creature - chained and clearly in huge amounts of distress was heartbreaking. Wewurukannala. should be shut down until Arjuna is released and sent to a sanctuary. I confronted one of the officials and he laughed - said it was because Arjuna is dangerous.it blows my mind that people are THIS STUPID. Please, I urge you not to go. It is heartbreaking and a side of Sri Lanka that is in the dark
title: ANIMAL ABUSE - THE STORIES ARE TRUE

body: The giant Buddha was impressive. But then i saw the distressed elephant chained on 3 legs, barely able to move more than sway. I cried. It made me sick. I tried talking to the guy who sold the tickets to find out what was happening with this poor elephant, but he was rude and dismissive. I’m not sure what to do to get this elephant rescued! I guess i would encourage folks to boycott this temple until they release the elephant.
title: The temple needs to free the chained elephant!!!

body: Terrible place and not a place to promote. The temple itself is interesting but the fact they’ve got an elephant tightly chained up in a small area. You can clearly see how distressed the animal is. Horrific cruelty.
title: Don’t visit

body: The temple and budda were very interesting however we were very distressed to see the poor elephant chained up and now wish we'd read the reviews first. We have spent time watching elephants in their natural environment so it was very confusing for our children to see this elephant in distress. I am not sure what to do about this but please this needs to stop and the elephant needs to be released into its natural environment
title: Don't go here, elephant chained in poor conditions

body: Can anyone please advise on the plight of the chained up elephant at the rear of this temple. We are deeply disappointed in the state and conditions of this poor creature
title: Cruelty

body: Terrible to see chained elephant, not being able to move, don’t think Buddha would approve it. Stop this nonsense, please.
title: Animal abuse

body: Very basic. It was okay seeing the big buddah. So that's worth maybe 2 stars.We where however thrilled, at first, to suddenly see an elephant at the back! We quickly came closer and suddenly excitement turned to utter disgust and heartbreak seeing the elephant chained up, swaying back and forth. It had chains on back and front feet exactly short enough that it can only be in one spot, not move forward. Not move to the sides. And not turn around. I am in love with Sri Lanka and everything we've seen so far. But this has got to stop. It was so sad seeing such a clever animal chained. Not being able to do anything but write this review. I hope this practice stops and both locals and tourist will take a stand against this. Had i known, I wouldn't have visited. We were encouraged by guides. So I hope you will read this review and change your mind. Truly.
title: Chained elephant

body: I really enjoyed my visit to Wewurukannala Vihara. The first thing that catches your eye is the massive seated Buddha — it’s breathtaking up close and something you won’t easily forget.The part that stood out most for me, though, was the “Tunnel of Hell.” It’s definitely unusual for a temple, with very vivid statues and murals showing the consequences of bad deeds. Honestly, it felt a bit unsettling at first, but at the same time it made me reflect on the teachings behind it. It’s not something you’ll see anywhere else.The rest of the temple has a lovely, authentic charm. The murals, smaller shrines, and the slightly worn but very real atmosphere give you a sense of local history and devotion. It isn’t overly polished or commercial, which I really liked.A couple of tips: dress modestly, as it’s a sacred site, and try to go early in the day or later in the afternoon when it’s cooler. Carry some water with you — the heat can be intense. There’s also a small fee/donation, which is fair considering how unique the experience is.All in all, I’d say Wewurukannala is well worth a visit if you’re in the south. It’s a mix of awe-inspiring, unusual, and thought-provoking. I’d happily stop by again if I’m in the area.
title: A Temple Full of Surprises!

body: We visited the temple with our guide, I was quite interested and then hugely disgusted to come across an elephant, chained up by the metal chains ,it was clearly distressed, and I was told it was "must".I find this wholly unacceptable and not in keeping with bhuddist teaching.
title: Disgusting day

body: We really wanted to go and see this temple area but after seeing pictures of the poor elephant that they keep there we decided that we should stay away.This treatment belongs way in the past (if at anytime at all). Certainly not in 2025. Maybe if tourists stay away they’ll get the message. Don’t go.
title: Don’t go. Cruelly keep an elephant chained up.

body: Chained Elephant in the backyard who‘s desperately Swimmingpool back and forth. We were crying to see this animal abuse 😭😭😭😭Please stop this cruelty. Its such a Beautiful Country but this was just heartbreaking and cruel 😭😭😭
title: Elephant being abused

body: An interesting temple with graphic murals depicting hell, the result of immoral acts during life.Ironically there is an immoral act playing out on site. There is an elephant chained to a small concrete pad. Having seen this our children were outraged and blind to all else for the rest of the visit.Care for the elephant properly please.
title: Chained elephant undercuts moral messaging.

body: During my travels from Ella to Ahangama, I had the opportunity to visit a few monasteries in the area. I chose this one as the 1st one with a particularly large Buddha statue.The road leading to the monastery was in good condition, with only a minor detour. The entry fee was 200 LKR per person, and we were asked to leave our shoes in the hall where the ticket collector was stationed.Upon entering, we were unexpectedly led through a "hell tunnel," which depicted graphic and horrifying punishments that await those who are sent to hell. As I had a toddler with me, I found some of these sculptures to be inappropriate for young children. This was an unexpected element to encounter in a monastery.We then proceeded to the Buddha statue, which was indeed impressive in size. However, it appeared to be in need of maintenance and was showing signs of age and wear.Below the statue, there were various other Buddha idols where people were worshipping. Unfortunately, there was also a chained elephant. Many visitors have given this place a one-star rating due to the presence of the elephant, and it was indeed saddening to see such a magnificent creature in captivity.Overall, it was an acceptable experience, but not one I would necessarily repeat.
title: Decent one time visit temple

body: An interesting temple to visit. Admission cost is 250 rupees per person. Definitely worthwhile going. What spoils this place is the poor elephant chained up by two of its legs so that it can only take a couple of steps back and forth. So cruel.
title: Cruelty to Elephant spoils visit.

body: As beautiful as the temple was, and as bizarre as the murals were, the little elephant that is marked down is completely dwarfed. Really very pathetic.
title: Chained elephant

body: Wewurukannala Buduraja Maha Viharaya located very close to the city dikwalla and this is must visit temple when you pass dikwalla area and large budda statue was mind relaxing. and there is a apaya we can see.
title: mind relaxing temple close to dikwalla city

body: It is a temple complex of a slightly different kind with the largest Buddha statue (50m high) in Sri Lanka. The temple complex is certainly not so impressive historically and the depictions of hell in the long corridor next to the temple but not for small children. Nevertheless, interesting and comparable to purgatory in Christianity.So far so good, but then we were actively pointed out an elephant as an “attraction”. We didn't have the words. Even if the treatment of elephants by locals is certainly not so “romantic”, this can only be described as cruel. Also during our visit the elephant was chained with minimal freedom of movement (+/- 1m) and even temporarily lay on a concrete/stone surface. Horrible, cruel, sad.... In this respect, take a picture of the Buddha, donate nothing and leave.The Buddha can be reached from Dickwella by Tuk Tuk in 10 minutes.
title: Interesting temple complex with cruel elephant keeping

body: How beautiful it was or not doesn't matter to this place. There's an elephant stuck in the heat with no room to move. It's sad and I hate that I spent money on it. Spend your time better and more fun!
title: Sad animal suffering

body: Located close to town. Entry for foreigners was 500rp but then you enter the temple and a caretaker insists on a donation from you. Then you go to hell tunnel and a caretaker insists on a donation there. I saw another guy inside a glassed office also showing a donation sign but I ignored him. Talk about double dipping.Inside the temple and the big buddha was the worthwhile attractions. Only took me about 20-25 minutes to look around.
title: Double dippers

body: The elephant is still chained under horrific conditions. Don’t go, it is not right to support this form of cruelty and I wish I could undo my visit. The elephant handlers seems wicked and harsh, very obvious that they do not care for the animal. We didn’t want to give them any money, which they reacted very unpleasant about.
title: Animal abuse

body: There's an elephant constantly tied up by its front and back legs, unable to move. It's pretty awful, the poor thing looks like it's really suffering, swaying back and forth.
title: Animal abusers

body: It was cruel... There was an elephant tied up by its hind leg... The chain was so short that it could only move about 1m and therefore always had to stand in its own feces and urine...I can't understand why there are still people who stand next to the elephant and have their photos taken...Please don't support this temple, maybe then attitudes will change...
title: Cruel treatment of elephants

body: If you are visiting the south of the island and interested in Buddhism and Buddhist Temples, this is a must see. Spend some time just sitting and meditating, connecting with yourself. Remarkable energy.
title: Peaceful. Serene.

body: Nice little temple visit as far as temples go with some good blessings. If you have time worth a visit but similar to all the temples in the area
title: Nice temple

body: Nice place to see, we were able to visit the temple inside, enter the hall of hell and offer our offerings
title: Sacred temple

body: This is a huge Buddhist stature that can go up to the structure by steps. it is a very old one and hope the temple is older than 250 years. There is a wall clock and it is also old nearly 250 years
title: Very good place to visit

body: A beautiful temple to visit. You can buy flowers for Budha from the lovely ladies at the entrance. The staff are very friendly and welcoming. Thank you!
title: A lovely temple to visit!

body: Beautiful Temple with lots of history, I was surprised how much there was to see inside also. It was very special.Although there are small donations expected for blessings etc it did not feel as overwhelming as other temples we visited and the man at the shoe basket actually refused a tip! Sadly there is an elephant chained up, it is had to accept this as part of their culture. Our guide didn’t see why were thought it was cruel. They genuinely cannot see why tourists would be horrified.
title: Beautiful temple

body: Temple the is quite striking when you walk towards it, definitely needs some TLC, take small currency as everyone has their hand out which is fine. I actually gave flower seller 500 rupees (£1.50) without taking the flowers and she was thrilled, beautiful people who really appreciate seeing foreigners.
title: Worth the walk...just

body: CRUELTY TO CHAINED UP ELEPHANT. Although the temple is beautiful, and has a reasonably priced enterance fee, there is an elephant chained up standing on a concrete platform in its own feces being shouted out and whipped for something as little as trying to cool itself with mud. Absolutely unacceptable. I understand the animals relevance to Budhism and importance to the temple and local people, but if this animal was sacred or respected in anyway it would not be treated as so, nor would they charge for a photo of such cruelty.
title: ANIMAL ABUSE

body: They keep a poor bull ELEPHANT CHAINED UP in the hot sun, the man keeping it was whipping the elephants back legs with a chain to make it move and the elephant was very obviously unhappy. Even when the elephant tried to get some water to cool himself off the keeper hit the elephant with a Stick to stop him taking the water, awful to see. I asked the men why they did this but they didn’t seem to speak English. The temple was nice, but I would urge you not to go and support this ill treatment of animals
title: CRUEL ANIMAL ABUSE

body: A nice walk to the temple, not to be missed. Very impressive buddhist temple. I love a huge room with a siiting and a laing Buddha. There is also a very impressive corridor with images about lessons in life. There is also a smaller Hindu room. I loved visiting Wewurukannala Vihara
title: not to be missed

body: This temple very famous as it is unique design with others. Climb to the top of the huge Buddha statue. The out side view is very beautiful after going to top. Can see Ancient temple with beautiful carvings
title: The one of the best Buddhist Temple

body: Beautiful. The maintainance could be a bit better, but the place is gorgeous and absolutely worth visiting.
title: BEAUTIFUL

body: Apart from the annoyance of being requested to pay at every corner of the temple, we were shocked about the chained Elephant. It couldn't move and was standing in his own excrements on a concrete platform! Please release the poor animal! This should not be allowed anywhere. Don't go and don't support this!!
title: Animal abuse

body: Warning: chained elephant to concrete slab. We did not know temple had a chained elephant until after we gave donations.
title: Chained Elephant

body: We were taken to visit the temple with our hotel driver who showed us around. It was interesting and the big buddha is very impressive. We had a blessing & offered a small donation. We were told about the 'elephant temple' which I assumed was a building, not an actual live elephant living in horrendous conditions. They were burning palm leaves about a foot from him and the smoke must've been in his eyes, causing even more distress. It was horrendous to see this beautiful creature chained on all legs, swaying back & forth. I was told he doesn't walk around, ever, unless there's a festival and he is 20 YEARS OLD. I will try to report this abuse but please be aware of what you are participating in, I wish I had done more research. There was also a dog with the worst mange I have ever seen, the monks do not care for these animals at all.
title: Interesting temple & buddha but horrifying animal abuse

body: Largest Buddha statue can be seen from afar. Entry ticket costs 200 LKR, additionally you’ll be asked for donation multiple times inside. Be ready to take your shoes off, knees and shoulders should be covered. The place is very beautiful, wall paintings are amazing, take your time to examine everything. There is also an elephant chained to the trees so tight that it can’t even move and just swinging all the time :(
title: Beautiful inside

body: You can enter for 200Rs, what is nothing. Then you need to buy flowers for 100Rs to give them to Lord Buddha. Then you can see many of Buddha statues and pictures of situations from his life. In old temple we've received a ritual to protect all family for free. We gave them a donation for the temple. Go there with a guide. Very nice place, I recommend that.
title: The temple with the power of stillness

body: I went with my 8yr old son. I’d found a tuk tuk driver, Sunil, who didn’t rip me off and we all went.Sunil very kindly have us the tour and it was amazing.The frescoes are in amazing condition, the sculptures were great.The whole story of Buddha is in front of you, the birth, the 55 lives etc.Really interesting.Lots of different little temples with further more intricate artwork.Climbing up with big Buddha was fun. Each floor had more frescoes. The breeze from the top was very welcomed as we went at midday - big error!Only points I’d give would be:Women take a sarong to cover your legsTake small not rupees to donate at the little temples.Give the ladies who seek flowers some money and make your offering.Don’t go at midday as you have to take you flip flops off and the ground is burning!
title: Amazing!

body: My wife, two grandchildren and I visited Wewurukannala Buddhist temple in the morning hours on 25th December 2019. The temple is famous for its 162 feet tall gigantic seated buddha statue. It is said to be the tallest seated Buddha statue in Sri Lanka. Being a holiday, there were many devotees visiting the temple. Foreign visitors are charged Rs 200 on entry. All visitors are required to dress modestly and leave their footwear at the entrance.The temple is in five parts.1. The oldest is the image house built in the late 18th century. Its outer face is intricately carved. The inner sanctum is dominated by sculpted buddha statues. In the area surrounding the inner sanctum are sculptures and paintings depicting Buddha’s life, surreal scenes depicting, gods, demons, princes, animals and others. 2. The second building demonstrates the “Hell” as Buddhists believe. People look at these sculptures with wide eyes imagining what it would be like in hell. There are graphic life-size sculptures of miscreants being sawn into pieces, dismembered, skinned, impaled on a spike, made to climb a tree with sharp thorns, eyes pulled out and many other torture details. Beware – be good to avoid having to go to hell!!3. There is a shrine room dedicated to god Skanda Kumara (Katharagama)4. At the upper level is the enormous, massive, gigantic seated buddha statue. There is also a bo-tree at the upper level. There were many devotees here at the upper level.5. The front of the museum has a large clock. Its working mechanism had initially been made of wood and is still on display. The wooden mechanism has now been replaced by a metal replica. The working mechanism of the clock with all its parts can be seen in the upper floor of the museum. The entrance fee to the museum is Rs.5. The time displayed in the clock was however incorrect.We spent about two hours in the temple premises and were rather amused by the gaudy creations at the “Buddhist Hell”.
title: Go - See - “Buddhist Hell”

body: "Amazing" place. After paying the admission fee, there are five different places that you can see. In each and every place, after saying "Ayubowan" to the person sitting there, we received exactly the same response "small donation please". But this is nothing compared to the elephant. It is year 2020 (no longer the Middle Ages) and elephant is still there, still chained, still in own excrement. So sad...
title: Elephant still there...

body: The most impressive is the large clock which can be seen from font of the the building. Inside, the mechanism of the clock is protected inside a glass cubicle.
title: Historical Buddhist temple

body: Captive elephant standing in it’s own urine and feces. What century are we living in people that this still happening? When I asked the local folk why they said that the road is close so they have to put a chain on both a back and a front foot to keep it “safe”. Literally the elephant couldn’t move in any direction! Horrifying. The Buddha itself is impressive. The surrounding temple is interesting but poorly maintained. The back rooms about hell and torture somewhat bizarre and not appropriate for kids. Paid Rs200 each to get in. Asked for tips / donations by another 3 separate men within the grounds again.
title: Captive elephant standing in its own urine and feces

body: It is Buddhist template with tallest Buddha statues in down south of Sri Lanka you must visit while when you are traveling to down south. it has a tallest wonderful Buddha statues that you can climb behind the statues.There are many Ancient attraction to see & worth time to spent time. one of attraction is OLD wall clock. it has big machine size of bed room.
title: It is Buddhist template with tallest Buddha statues in down south of Sri Lanka you must visit

body: Amazing temple with huge Buddhas. I have to say that I am a temple addict, but this temple is fantastic.200Rs to get in for foreigners.A must see if you are in Dickwekla or around.
title: Great temple

body: The temple itself is incredible but I was horrified to see the temple elephant chained up by a both its front and rear right legs, unable to move an inch. The abuse is utterly disturbing and the elephant is clearly distressed rocking back and forward. The local tourism businesses that are thriving on international visitors should take some responsibility to help end this abuse. This is truely disgraceful and should not be supported. I will report this abuse but I don’t imagine that will have much impact, change will only come if local operators stop turning a blind eye to what is happening in their backyard.
title: Outrageous Animal Abuse

body: Actually three parts, the first two are most interesting. The 17th-18th century original structure is beautifully painted and ornately decorate. The "Hell Tunnel" is a macabre trip illustrated with frescoes and plaster monsters tormenting people in Hell. The Buddha is the largest in Sri Lanka, reportedly, but we didn't go in there. 200 rupees.
title: Bizarre Temple

body: Do not visit or support this temple. Yes, the Buddha is nice - but what isn't ... is the temple elephant chained up in the back of the temple. Chained front to back .. this poor creature cannot move 1 foot in any direction. It is chained into a permanent stance for the rest of its life ... just stuck there on a concrete pad in obvious distress. Please do not visit this temple and support this cruelty.
title: Animal Abuse at it's best

body: My husband had not seen this Temple before - I last visited it 20 years ago on my way to Yala. It is definitely an eye opener when it comes to Buddhism!! I understand they have to preserve the paintings and depictions of "sinful living" but now to change them to concrete is a bit sad. Maybe the authorities could have come up with repainting? The paintings were only painted in the 1980's so a more thoughtful and aesthetic solution should maybe have been more looked into. Anyway, it was an interesting visit and one of the local keepers of the Temple was more than keen to show us around - without being too pushy. My Sri Lankan husband loved this Temple.....and that is a big thing as he is no Culture - Vulture!
title: Wonderfully Bizarre

body: This is a very colourful temple situated in Dickwella . Easy access. On the way to famous Mulgirigala temple.
title: A colourful temple

body: Impressive temple from 18th century with highest Buddha statue in Sri Lanka ( 50m ! ). Inside of temple there are tens of statues picturing sinners and demons. One of my personal favorites of whole Island. Also low entrance price.
title: Temple with largest Buddha statue in Sri Lanka

body: Wewurukannala Temple, Near dickwella houses Sri Lanka’s tallest seated Buddha statue.. 150-feet tall. Built in the 1960’s it does have a less ancient, and more psychedelic decor. This reclining Buddha was in one of the attached image houses, as was the “Hall-of-Horrors” “Hall-of-Punishments”, which definitely warrants separate postings! (stay tuned). .
title: 60’s Kitsch + Hall-of-Punishment = MUST SEE

body: Came here while travelling along the south cost. Was not expecting much but was pleasantly surprised. Beautiful structure filled with local people, not so many tourists. Costs only 200LkR to go in, Budda is in pretty good condition and you can go inside in while there are many beautiful frescoes.The only disappointing part was the fact that there is an elephant chained up by the back foot with a 2 meter chain, was very sad to see this. If it was not for the elephant, the score would have been higher. Please move this elephant to somewhere more comfortable, perhaps to national park only 50km away.
title: Much better than expected

body: I am really wondering about this place and you must visited here. Lot of tourists and local being here everytime. And the other special thing is this is the one of famous historical valuable Buddhist temple around in southern coast -Matara.
title: Most respected...

body: Wonderful old temple. We have been told, that the temple is 2500 yrs old, there are a lots of sculptures about the ancient times of buddhism. It worst a visit if you are in the area, this temple is different to an average buddhist temple, there are a lot more to see inside.
title: Wonderful old temple worst a visit

body: Do not go, unless you want to fund animal cruelty. There is an elephant chained and it can’t move and it is seemingly stressed and in agony. The visit made me sad.
title: Beautiful temple but terrible animal cruelty

body: The temple itself is ok. It was quite sad seeing the chained elephant; apparently he is 22 and he has been chained for 12 years or so.I would recommend the Rock Temple instead.
title: It’s OK

body: Can only agree with others on this one. The people who run this must take such criticism on board. No justification for keeping this animal chained up like this. Shame.
title: Shocked to see how the elephant is kept

body: Taken here by Tuk Tuk, loved the cartoons depicting sins and then apparently all is forgiven. The attitude of the Buddhists never ceases to amaze. Whatever floats yiur boat, you can only hope your after life does not include any of this form of torture! Be careful of those wanting to give you a tour,
title: Facinating

body: Budu Raja Maha Wehera Wewurukannala Buddhist temple in Dickwella is a very impressive sight. The literature on site claims the Buddha statue is the largest in Asia. It certainly is impressively big. The shrine room is 350 years old and contains a reliquary of the Buddha's tooth. I'm glad I made the stop. One most remove one's shoes prior to entering the complex, and there is a minimal entrance fee.
title: Impressive Temple

body: This place is worth the time just to see the first temple. It’s on the right as you pay at the desk. We paid 300 rupees each. We were asked for a donation on the temple also. It really was stunning inside. Giant statues of Buddha and many other large carvings all very old and colourful. Beautiful history & there were only a few other tourists. The other temples on site are much more modern and we did not find them interesting. We climbed the internal stairs in the big Buddha statue but there was not much of a view. Worth 30 mins in the old, first temple though.
title: One amazing temple

body: new, not nice, durty, no welcome, all that with an entry ticket. . useless visit! basically, nothing interesting to see in the surroundings!!
title: not worth a visit!!

body: We visited the temple on Poya day and were excited to explore the site among worshippers on a holy day. However, our visit was ruined when we saw an elephant chained up (both front and back), rocking back and forth in obvious distress, standing in its own excrement on a concrete slab not much larger than the size of a large car. It is absolutely unconscionable to keep a large animal in such deplorable conditions. Unfortunately we were not aware of the situation and had already paid an entry fee (200 LKR per person). Please reconsider visiting this temple and contributing to this horrible, archaic practice. TripAdvisor should remove this listing.
title: Disappointed to see our tourist dollars spent on keeping elephant in captivity

body: We didn't enjoy our visit here. The large buddha was quite impressive but there was elephant that was chained up in a really cruel way. It was not in line with Buddhist ideology in my opinion at all. He was chained on a front and a back leg and there was no slack in the chains so he couldn't move. Really sad.
title: Chained up elephant looked really sad

body: This temple is certainly worth visiting. The climb to the top of the Buddha statue is rewarded with great views and a close-up look at Buddha’s hair. The graphic depictions of the hell realms may be somewhat confronting but the saddest part of the visit is seeing the beautiful, sensitive temple elephant cruelly chained so that it cannot move, cannot even take one step! He is kept in his own hell realm. There are wonderful places to see elephants behaving normally, eg Uda Walawe National Park, but please avoid being part of the abuse of these wonderful beings. Last year, TripAdvisor stopped selling tickets to the cruelest wildlife tourist attractions, some include elephant riding. Well done Tripadvisor! See worldanimalprotection.org for more info.
title: Wewurukannala Vihara, Dikwella

body: Take the climb to the top of the Buddha and see the 550 frescos documenting the many reincarnations...
title: Magnificent

body: This place is beautiful! Amazing 50m high buddha and beautiful history throughout the site. We visited in June and had the place to ourselves. A must see when in the Dikwella area!
title: Stunning

body: A great heritage temple - a must see! Superb architecture, clean and well maintained. A very spiritual moment full of colors and flowers. Remember to cover your shoulders and avoid shorts.
title: Superb location

body: when you reach the top, you have a panoramic view. im not that much religious but its still a temple. it lets you to climb up doesn't mean its not a temple. so behave yourself.
title: Panoramic view...

body: Nice big statue....paid 200R. There was no one helpfull and no english sign so I didnt know where to go...i saw just very sad elephant -tied around his legs to the pole so he could not move!!! So bad and sad!!!
title: Very sad elephant :-(

body: We loved our trip here. The temple was quiet and seemed well off the tourist trail. The beautifully coloured carvings and giant Buddha statue made for much to discuss with our two boys aged 8 and 10. You can climb all the way to the top of the Buddha's head through stairwells filled with pictorial paintings detailing events in the life of the Buddha. We spent around 1 1/2 hours here and really enjoyed the experience. The only negative was seeing the chained elephant in/near the temple grounds. Entrance is only around 200rs per adult.
title: Peaceful and interesting half day trip

body: If you're in the area, do visit this temple to see the gruesome and kitschy frescoes that illustrate in a more Christian than Buddhist fashion that hell one will endure for not following the Buddhist ways. I would agree with another reviewer that this is not an essential site, and again with another reviewer that it would be nice to free the chained elephant. But, if you're in the area, I would recommend dropping by.
title: Worth it for the Kitschy Frescoes

body: We were brought to this temple by our driver on the way from Mirissa to Ella. He stopped and in his rather limited English told us to visit the temple.Undoubtedly it was a pleasant surprise! At the entrance we were offered to buy some flowers for Bodha ad we did it. Then we visited as much as we could in rather short time and I am so sorry that we couldn't find a professional guide at the spot. My advice for all travelers that are in vicinity: DO visit this temple but be sure to be accompanied by a professional guide. Otherwise it would be a series of many many intriguing and fascinating sculptures and wall paintings with no sense at all. We had hundreds of questions ... but unfortunately they remained without an answer.
title: Don't visit without a professional guide!

body: An amazing and terrifying place! We loved the beautiful ancient temple and the glorious Buddha. The "hell" section was a real eye-opener and we spent a long time walking this section which depicts various punishments that are applied for actions. Graphic and compelling, and perhaps not for young kids who are likely to be freaked out by some of the statues and pictures. Well worth a visit.
title: Take you time to soak up the various sections

body: This temple has a 50m high seated Buddha statue from the late 1960's. You can apparently climb to the top of the Buddha from behind but not the day we were there - don't know why. The main image house has strange statues at the front and an awful long corridor of gruesome paintings depicting the various punishments inflicted on sinners for each sin. I didn't think Buddhists did this. Catholics yes, but Buddhists? There is even a very gross punishment for forgetting to remove your slippers at the temple. Ouch - guilty!

body: We took a taxi here from Tangalle and visited a few other local attractions as part of an ad hoc 1/2 day tour. It was actually more interesting than I had expected. It is quite a bizarre place as in addition to the huge buddha (you can climb up and go into the back of his head!!) there are lots of murals and statues depicting scenes from both Buddhas life and also the punishments that will be meted out to this who sin. It was grotesquely medieval but fascinating to see....the message was clear though, be good or else!! Well worth a visit!

body: Some free time during my stay at Dikwella resort brought me to this ancient temple which had been built back in 1780's. The most prominent feature is that it has this amazing 160 ft tall gold plated seating Buddha statue which is the first sight appearing from a considerable distance as you reaching the location.It has the most ancient clock in Sri Lanka built by W Elaris Desilva which is known as the first locally made in the history of SL. The Miusium is a must see place for all who visit Wewurukannala.There is a separate section where you find structures of demands punishing sinners who do not follow the path of enlightenment as taught in the Buddhist religion. It is a considerably long cave like path where everyone visits, where there are many wall paintings of the consequences of not following the teachings of lord Buddha. Its purpose if to create fear so I do not recommend to small children to visit with their parents.All in all, its a very interesting place to be and many things you can learn about Buddhism (specially in the "Budhu Ge").
title: One of the best ancient temples

body: I love it that you have to remove your shoes/flip flops when entering the temple ground. Walking barefoot can be tricky in the heat though as the rocks are burning! Be warned. The Temple has a big buddha. You can climb up to his shoulder at the back of the statue where the stairs are. There is a tunnel which you can walk through with drawings of hell on the walls. A little bit depressing, but definitely interesting. What I found most beautiful about the place was the main hall with all the statues and segments from the the life of buddha showed in huge statues and art pieces. Don't forget to buy a flower at the entrance so you can place this one in the main hall as an offer. Get blessed not just by buddha, but also by the hindi gods in one of the smaller buildings. I didn't like the elephant. I feel very sorry for the poor creature as it is always chained with just a small possibility of movement.

body: When you drive up you can't help but notice the 50m tall statute of a sitting Buddha. There is a entrance fee of Rs200 per person - need to remove shoes, hats and women need to cover legs. First stop is the main shrine room, which contains numerous statues of Buddha, Kings, demons and monks - spend your time here fully exploring the rooms and taking in the murals/frescos on the walls & ceilings.Next near the white stupa is a cave/tunnel (tunnel of hell) a series of wall paintings depicting the punishments for wrongdoers- which is fun but not particularly enlightening.Then you need to take in the giant Buddha statue, which is covered in shiny mosaic tiles.If you are lucky, like we were, you might get to see the temple elephant having a bath and a scrub. She enjoys being hand fed bananas or biscuits but expect her handlers to ask for a small gratuity.

body: The temple's most obvious feature is the 50m tall statue of Buddha. However we much enjoyed the 'tunnel of terror' depicting in statues and cartoons what happens to sinners: being sawn in half, dismembered, boiled in a large cauldron etc. Most appealing to us as the temple building with many statues of Buddha in his various positions as well as of kings, worshipers and monks. Very colorful, very visual. There is a foreigner entrance fee of 200 rupee, which also entitles you to take pictures. When we visited, we were the only foreigners, which made us stand out among the local worshipers.
title: Buddha temple worth the detour

body: This is an ancient temple and very special place to worship by the Buddhists in Sri Lanka. There is a huge seated Buddha statue which supposed to be built several hundred years ago. I think this must be the largest Buddha statue in Sri Lanka. There are several interesting places we must see. one is the "Tunnel of Hell". It demonstrate the punishment to the wrong doers according to Buddha's teaching. Some as pictures drawn on the walls of the tunnel, some given as verses written in "Sinhala". Also there are several life size statues of "King Yama" , his soldiers and wrong doers demonstrating how they punish for the wrong done. Some displays cutting the wrong doer in to two with a saw, some forcing to climb the tree of "Katu Imbula" ( a tree with sharp edges) , some drawn in boiling cauldrons etc., Also there are several statues "King Suprabudda", "Devadatta Thero" "Chinchi Manavika" etc showing that they were half drawn inside the earth and going to the hell since they have done " Ananthariya Papakarma" (means five most dangerous sins, Shedding blood of Buddha, Killing Rahath Thero, Spliting Sanga, Killing Mother, Killing Father).Inside the shrine room there are lot of paintings and statutes displaying various events of Buddha's life from birth to "Parinirvana" (death).Also the temple has a museum which is a must see place if you visit there. There is a large clock of which the mechanism is made out of wooden originally but now it is in metal. the wooden mechanism with wheels in displayed inside a glass cubical. The clock supposed to be very old made by a local craftsman. Rs. 5/- is charged from each to see the museum.The most colorful event in the calendar is the Temple "Perahera" (Procession ) with lot of elephants and dancers.
title: Very Ancient Temple

We had a fun time trying to decipher the different paintings (2 adults and a boy of 9), and we all found it hillarios. Even the quite explicit torturemethods we found funny. title: Unintentionally hilarious
body: As others have noted, the Buddha here is huge, and worth a look (and yes, you'll have to pay- 200 rupees to enter per person, then a donation to enter other buildings. Seems fair enough). The first temple you'll see has a gallery of various life-sized figures set around an inner sanctum with a reclining Buddha and a larger standing one, resplendent in the murky light. The second you enter to scenes of torture, showing you what may happen if you stray from the true path. This may involve being sawn in two, nastily impaled on a spike, or dunked head-down in boiling oil. All of this by a bunch of mischievous Devils who seem to be having the time of their lives. Leading off this is a seemingly endless corridor with more murals of the same- the crime in the picture above (which you'll have to guess at if you don't read Sinhalese), the punishment below (mainly self-explanatory, mainly gruesome, mainly involving impaling, boiling oil or random dismemberment. Fun.)The standing Buddha outside is large, and unfortunately, if your imagination has been fired by all the rest, seems to have a dollop of ice cream on his head, and only lacks a 99 Flake.

title: Big, bigger and biggest
body: There are many big Buddha statues all over Sri Lanka. This is the biggest and certainly impressive. No shoes allowed. You pay Rs100 entry fees. The temple also features interesting and colorful statues.The turnoff to the temple from A2 is right in the town of Dikwella heading towards Beliatta. Pass through some houses and shops about 1-1.5km and veer left, the big Buddha would be the 1st sight. Wow!

title: Fabulous and grand in the morning
body: This place is easy to get to by tuk-tuk either from Dickwella or Matara. I highly recommend doing that because walking back was deadly hot and I was even happy when a passing yuk-tuk suggested to give me a ride to Dickwella center. You have to bargain with them. Don't agree to ride unless it's a half from the initial price, at least. And don't sit in the car, unless you've agreed on a price. The guy was so eager to have me as his customer, he said "it OK" when I asked him about the price. But when he realized that he's not getting paid at all unless we agree on it now, he gave up.The place itself is great but it's the best to go there in the morning when there's not so many tourists. Also, since it's a working temple, try to be quiet and respectful of the locals who come here to pray. Take off your shoes before the steps to the territory.You can also get a tour around the premises for an additional price. But it's up to you. Locals will try to sell you absolutely everything. Go for it only after you've seen what there is to see and want some additional info.Overall, I really enjoyed visiting this place! I came there to draw the tallest statue of Buddha in Sri Lanka, and was happy to go back with a result:http://www.flickr.com/photos/natavision/8274987576
